Permission denied

Description:
A permission denied error occurs when the Docker client or daemon does not have permission to access a required resource.

Common Cause:
The current user may not have the required permissions to communicate with the Docker daemon or access a file.

Troubleshooting:
Check the permissions associated with the resource.
Verify that the Docker daemon is running.
Check the Docker installation and user configuration.

Port is already allocated

Description:
This error occurs when Docker attempts to publish a container port that is already being used by another process or container.

Common Cause:
Another application or container is already listening on the requested host port.

Troubleshooting:
Identify the process or container using the port.
Stop the conflicting process or container if appropriate.
Alternatively, configure the container to use a different host port.

Cannot connect to the Docker daemon

Description:
This error occurs when the Docker client cannot communicate with the Docker daemon.

Common Cause:
The Docker daemon may not be running or the client may be configured to communicate with an unavailable daemon.

Troubleshooting:
Verify that the Docker daemon is running.
Check the Docker installation.
Verify the Docker client configuration and connection settings.

No such file or directory

Description:
Docker may report this error when a referenced file or directory cannot be found.

Common Cause:
A path may be incorrect, a file may not exist, or a file may not be available in the expected build or container context.

Troubleshooting:
Verify that the referenced file exists.
Check the path for spelling errors.
Verify the build context and volume paths.

MODULE_NOT_FOUND

Description:
MODULE_NOT_FOUND occurs when Node.js cannot locate a module that an application is attempting to load.

Common Cause:
The required package may not be installed, the module path may be incorrect, or the application may be running from an unexpected directory.

Troubleshooting:
Check that the required package is installed.
Verify the module name and import path.
Check the current project directory.
If the package is a dependency, verify that it is listed in package.json and installed.

TypeError

Description:
TypeError occurs when a JavaScript operation is performed on a value of an inappropriate type.

Common Cause:
A variable may contain an unexpected value such as null or undefined, or an operation may not be valid for the value's type.

Troubleshooting:
Inspect the value and its type before performing the operation.
Check whether the value is null or undefined.
Verify that function arguments have the expected types.

ReferenceError

Description:
ReferenceError occurs when JavaScript attempts to access a variable or identifier that is not available in the current scope.

Common Cause:
The variable may not have been declared, may be misspelled, or may be outside the current scope.

Troubleshooting:
Check the spelling of the identifier.
Verify that the variable has been declared.
Check the scope in which the variable is being accessed.

SyntaxError

Description:
SyntaxError occurs when JavaScript code does not follow the language syntax expected by the parser.

Common Cause:
The code may contain a missing bracket, parenthesis, quotation mark, or another syntax problem.

Troubleshooting:
Inspect the line identified by the error.
Check brackets, parentheses, and quotation marks.
Verify that the surrounding code follows valid JavaScript syntax.

NullPointerException

Description:
NullPointerException occurs when an application attempts to use a reference that contains null in a way that requires an actual object.

Common Cause:
An object reference may not have been initialized or a method may have returned null.

Troubleshooting:
Identify which reference is null.
Check where the reference is initialized.
Verify whether a method can return null before using its result.
Add appropriate null checks where required.

ClassNotFoundException

Description:
ClassNotFoundException occurs when an application attempts to load a class by name but the class cannot be found.

Common Cause:
The required class may not be available on the application's classpath.

Troubleshooting:
Verify that the required dependency is present.
Check the application's classpath.
Verify the package and class name.
Check whether the required dependency was included during compilation or execution.

ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException

Description:
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException occurs when code attempts to access an array using an index outside the valid range.

Common Cause:
The index may be negative or greater than or equal to the array length.

Troubleshooting:
Check the array length.
Verify the index before accessing the array.
Remember that Java array indexes begin at zero.

NumberFormatException

Description:
NumberFormatException occurs when a string cannot be converted into the requested numeric type.

Common Cause:
The input string may contain characters or formatting that are not valid for the expected numeric representation.

Troubleshooting:
Inspect the input string.
Verify that it contains a valid numeric representation.
Handle invalid input before attempting conversion.

ModuleNotFoundError

Description:
ModuleNotFoundError occurs when Python cannot find the module that a program is trying to import.

Common Cause:
The required package may not be installed in the Python environment currently being used.

Troubleshooting:
Check whether the required package is installed in the active Python environment.
For example, if a program imports the requests package, verify that requests is installed in the environment.

Another possible cause is that the program is being executed with a different Python interpreter or virtual environment from the one where the package was installed.

NameError

Description:
NameError occurs when Python encounters a name that has not been defined.

Common Cause:
A variable, function, or other name may be misspelled or may not have been defined before it is used.

Troubleshooting:
Check the spelling of the variable or function name.
Verify that the name has been defined before the line where it is used.

TypeError

Description:
TypeError occurs when an operation or function is applied to an object of an inappropriate type.

Common Cause:
The program may be trying to perform an operation using incompatible data types.

Troubleshooting:
Check the types of the values involved in the operation.
Verify that function arguments have the expected types.

IndexError

Description:
IndexError occurs when a sequence is accessed using an index that is outside the valid range.

Common Cause:
The program may be trying to access an element at an index that does not exist.

Troubleshooting:
Check the length of the list or sequence.
Make sure the index is within the valid range.

KeyError

Description:
KeyError occurs when a dictionary is accessed using a key that does not exist in the dictionary.

Common Cause:
The requested key may be missing from the dictionary.

Troubleshooting:
Check whether the key exists before accessing it.
Verify that the key is spelled correctly.
